intro: Written in a few hours in April 1962 and sung at Gerde's Folk City the same month, before he had even finished it to his liking. Within a year it was an anthem — first in other people's voices.

lives.title: An old spiritual underneath
lives.note: The tune draws on "No More Auction Block", a spiritual sung by people escaping slavery. His own Gaslight Cafe performance of it from 1962 later came out on The Bootleg Series Vol. 1–3.

lives.title: First time out
lives.note: The earliest performance on record, in an early form of the song.

lives.title: The Freewheelin' recording
lives.note: Just voice, guitar and harmonica. Released in May 1963 as the opening track of The Freewheelin' Bob Dylan.

lives.title: Peter, Paul and Mary
lives.note: Their harmony version reached number two in the US in summer 1963 and made the song known well beyond the folk clubs.

lives.title: Newport finale
lives.note: The festival closed with Dylan, Joan Baez, Peter, Paul and Mary, Pete Seeger and the Freedom Singers singing it together, arm in arm.

lives.title: Slow and gospel-tinged
lives.note: Re-arranged for the 1978 big band with backing singers, slowed down and almost hymn-like. On Bob Dylan at Budokan.

lives.title: Live Aid
lives.note: The last song of his short acoustic set with Keith Richards and Ronnie Wood, seen around the world.

lives.title: The late encore
lives.note: From 2012 to 2019 it was a regular encore, rearranged several times and often led from the piano.

others.note: Didn't record a hit version, but said the song spurred him to write "A Change Is Gonna Come".
A soul version that went top ten in the US.
